A Hall building's `accusative` is its plain name; the sentences put "the" before it ("Donate to the Banner?"). The forms after a number (attackForms, trialForms, counted, pieceForms…) are [one, other, other] for the Polish [one, few, many]. Guild roles: lider leader, zastępca deputy. The Exchange's button „Wymień” is “Exchange”.

texts.title: Guild Hall
texts.intro: The Hall's buildings give bonuses to every guild member. You donate gold and resources to the building you choose yourself.
how: The guild has no common purse. From character level {level}, each member donates their own gold and resources to the building they choose. Donations are not returned, even after leaving the guild.

Each building grows from zero to level {max}. It reaches the next level when the donations to it cover the whole cost of that level: the gold and the resource. Whatever you donate beyond the cost carries over to the next level.
The first level costs {firstGold} gold and {firstResource} of the resource, and each one after it costs more, up to {lastGold} gold and {lastResource} of the resource at level {max}.
The leader and deputies can mark buildings as preferred, so the guild knows what to save up for now. It is only a hint: you donate to whatever you like.
The bonuses work for every guild member. An exploration takes them from the moment it sets out, and the Anvil from the moment of upgrading. After leaving the guild, the bonuses are gone.

texts.title: Temple
texts.intro: In the Temple your guild picks a patron every week. The god who wins the vote gives every member a bonus for the whole next week.
how: Three gods are on offer every week. Every member casts one vote, until Sunday midnight. A vote cannot be changed.

On Monday at midnight the god with the most votes wins. In a tie, the god the leader voted for wins; if the leader voted for none of them, the one that reached that many votes first. If nobody votes, the guild has no patron for the week.

The patron gives every guild member a bonus for the whole week, like the Weeks: an exploration and a profession's work take the bonus of the moment they began, and the Anvil of the moment of upgrading. Whoever joins the guild during the week has the bonus at once, and whoever leaves loses it.
That week half of the trials on the Trials board are from the patron's domain and bear its sign.
The Temple stands in the Hall from the start and has no levels.

texts.title: Guild Expedition
texts.lead: The members' exploration minutes lead the guild through {stages} stages. At the end of each stage a guardian bars the way.
how: Every week, from Monday at midnight, the guild sets out on a new route through the land at the average level of its active members, that is, those whose account was in the game in the last {days} days.
Every minute of a guild member's exploration moves the route on once they claim the report. Quick Hunts and Party explorations count too.
A stage is {perMember} minutes of exploration for each active guild member.
A guardian waits at the end of a stage. The route stands still until the guild defeats it. Minutes gathered in the meantime wait and move the route on right after it falls.
Everyone who added minutes this week attacks the guardian: {attacks} times a day, separately from the attacks on the Beast. An attack is one fight with full HP and no potions.
Each next guardian is stronger. A defeated one gives a chest to everyone who added minutes this week. The last one also gives rare loot: an item of your class.
A defeated guardian also gives the guild Fame in the Ranking: {fame} for each one, and {fameLast} for the last.
You can claim the chest until the end of next week.

texts.title: Guild Beast
texts.lead: Every week the whole guild hunts one beast. The damage stays on its shared HP bar.
rules: The beast is the champion of one of the lands, at the guild members' average level. The more members, the more HP it has.
Each character attacks {attacks} times a day, separately from the entries to the Towers. New attacks come at midnight.
An attack is one fight with full HP and no potions, with the result at once. It gives no XP, gold or loot. You can attack during an exploration, too.
The beast stays until Sunday midnight. On Monday a new one comes.

Every guild member gets a Beast Chest, even without attacking. It counts everyone who was in the guild when the beast came or joined before it fell. If the beast falls, the chest holds an item of the character's class at their level and the beast's materials.
If the beast survives the week, the chest holds only materials: the more of the bar the guild took off, the more of them (from 25, 50 and 75%). Below 25% there is no chest.
You can open the chest from the beast's fall or from the end of the week, until the end of the next week at the latest.

texts.title: Guild Trials
texts.intro: Every day more trials from all over the game appear on the board. They all count at once: you complete them in ordinary play, and the guild draws closer to the chests.
how: Trials need not be taken: all of those on the board count at once. What you do in ordinary play advances every matching trial from the moment it appears on the board, and its numbers suit your character's level.

On Monday the board has {first} trials, and every day {daily} new ones are added. At most {perDay} of your trials go onto the guild's bar for each day of the week: {twoDays} in all by Tuesday, {threeDays} by Wednesday, and so on. Those completed beyond that will go onto the bar on the following days.
The members' completed trials fill a shared bar with {thresholds} thresholds. Each threshold reached gives a chest to everyone who completes at least one trial this week.

The thresholds grow with the number of active members, that is, those whose account was in the game in the last {days} days, counted when the board is drawn. Whoever joins later raises the thresholds in part: the fewer days left until Sunday, the less.
The chest holds gold, Time Points and the material of creatures from the place your class goes to. The last four thresholds also give System Points.
You can claim the chest until the end of next week. A new board comes on Monday at midnight.

texts.title: Guild Requests
texts.intro: Short of a material, herb, potion, mineral or scroll? Ask the guild, and others will give from their stores.
how: You can have one request up at a time, for up to {most} of one material, herb, potion, mineral or scroll. You can add the next one {wait} hours after the previous. You can withdraw a request no one has given anything to yet and add a new one at once.
A request stays up until someone fills it, until you withdraw it, or for {open} hours. The pieces given come to you at once, with the giver's name, and you thank each gift with a single tap.

Herbs and potions go to the bag, so they need room in it. You cannot ask for items or gold. The Encyclopedia will not count the pieces given: only what the character obtains or makes on their own counts.
Giving brings no gold or System rewards. It counts towards the Benefactors of the week ranking and the Guild Trials. Characters of one account do not give each other anything.

texts.title: Help with builds and work
texts.intro: Help your guild's members: every help shortens their build or their work in a profession.
how: Here you see the builds in the Camp and the Stronghold and the profession work of your guild's members. Every member can help, except characters of the same account.
Each help shortens a build or a work by {share}% of its time, but at least by {min}. One build or work takes at most {max} helps, and you help with it once.
For each help you get {perHelp} of Fame for the guild, at most {cap} a week. The week starts on Monday at midnight.
A yellow dot by the Guild tab means someone needs help. “Help everyone” helps at once with every build and work you still can.
At the top you see your own build and work, with the names of those who helped you.

texts.title: Resource exchange
texts.intro: Too much stone and too little wood? Post an offer, and someone in the guild will take it. You can also sell and buy resources for gold. You can exchange fish, crops and dishes from the Pantry too.
how: An offer is pieces of one resource for pieces of another, or a resource for gold and gold for a resource: from 1 to {most} pieces of a resource and from 1 to {goldMost} gold. {counts}
From the Pantry you can exchange fish, crops and dishes: for resources, for gold or for other goods from the Pantry, from 1 to {most} pieces.
The pieces you give leave your resources, your gold or your Pantry at once and wait in the offer.
An offer is taken whole. Whoever taps “Exchange” gives what you want and gets what you give. Your part comes to you at once.
You can post at most {offers} at a time. Each stays up for at most {open}, and you can withdraw it at any moment.
The pieces of an offer come back to you whole when you withdraw it, when its time runs out, or when you leave the guild.
Characters of one account do not exchange with each other.

texts.title: Guild Chest
texts.intro: Leave an item in the chest, and someone from the guild takes it when they look in. You do not have to play at the same time.
how: Put an item from your bag in for everyone or for one character of the guild. A worn item cannot go in.
An item for everyone can be taken by any guild member except novices (R1). An item for one character can be taken only by them, and while it waits, you can take it back.
The chest holds {capacity}. To take an item, you need room in your bag.
Items go in and come out from character level {level}, as in the Exchange. You can take your own item back before that too.
An item keeps its upgrade, gem, rarity and Tier. The Encyclopedia does not count an item from another character.
“Recent moves” show up to {log}: who puts in or takes out what, and when.
When someone leaves the guild, the items for them are for everyone from then on. The last character can leave the guild only once the chest is empty.

how: Every week the guilds play a league, each against each. From Monday, every evening at {hour} your guild plays a match against the next guild until it has played them all. With an odd number of guilds, one has each round off, each guild once a week. With more than 8 guilds, some evenings have two matches.

A match is 1v1 and 3v3 fights: every member of your guild fights every member of the rival guild, and every trio fights every rival trio. The game draws the trios at midnight, for the whole day: one who joins during the day fights only the 1v1 that evening, and one who leaves leaves an empty place in the trio. A trio short of members fights with fewer. There are as many 3v3 fights as if both guilds had the trios of the bigger one: each trio the smaller guild lacks loses by walkover to every rival trio. For example, 6 trios against 10 make 100 fights: 60 are fought and the smaller guild gives 40 by walkover.
Characters fight as they are saved, as in the Arena, without companions or mercenaries.
The table counts the fights won and lost over the whole week, walkovers included.

On Sunday at {hour} the league ends. 1st place collects {first} and {firstItems} of champion rarity for the Guild Chest, 2nd place {second} and {secondItems}, and 3rd place {third}. A place brings its prize only when someone is below it in the table.
For every fight you win you collect {gold} gold, and for a won match you fought in, {systemPoints}.

texts.endPrize: Your guild took place {place} and collected {fame} and a war chest: {items} in the Guild Chest.
texts.endFame: Your guild took place {place} and collected {fame}.
texts.yourDuels: In the 1v1 you fight every member of the rival guild.
texts.walkoversOurs: The rival has more trios. Each trio your guild lacks loses by walkover to every rival trio: {count} in all.
texts.walkoversTheirs: Your guild has more trios. Each trio the rival lacks loses by walkover to every one of your trios: {count} in all.
texts.voidLine: A match without fights: one of the sides had nobody to fight.
texts.doneAll: Your guild has played all its matches. The league ends on Sunday at {hour}.
texts.noFights: This match had no fights: walkovers only.

texts.lead: Fame is the guild's points for what its members do together. The week starts on Monday at midnight.
how: Guild Beast: {beastPercent} for each full 1% of the week's beast bar, and {beastFell} for its fall.
Guild Expedition: {perGuardian} for each guardian defeated, and {lastGuardian} for the seventh, the last.
Guild Trials: {perTrial} for each trial completed. At most {trialCap} trials count from one character, as on the Trials bar.
Guild Requests: {perPiece} for each piece given to a guild member. At most {giftCap} pieces count from one character.
Exchange: {perExchange} for each exchange. At most {exchangeCap} exchanges count from one character that takes offers.
Help with builds and work: {perHelp} for each help. At most {helpCap} helps a week count from one character.
“All time” is the Fame of all the weeks, this one included.
The guild with the most Fame in the previous week has a gold tag for the whole week. In a tie, the older guild wins.
texts.howWar: Guild war league: {warFirst} for 1st place in the week, {warSecond} for 2nd and {warThird} for 3rd.
texts.champion: Best guild of the previous week

members.title: Members' ranking
members.tap: Tap a member to see where their Fame comes from.
members.lead: Here you can see how much Fame each member brought the guild and how much they donated to the Hall. Every point of Fame also gives a Guild Mark, and the best of the week become Heroes of the week.
how: Guild Beast: {beastPercent} for each full 1% of the bar the member knocked off, and {beastFell} for the final blow.
Guild Expedition: {perGuardian} for each guardian defeated, and {lastGuardian} for the seventh. The points are shared by the damage dealt to the guardian.
Guild Trials: {perTrial} for each trial completed, at most {trialCap} trials a week.
Guild Requests: {perPiece} for each piece given, at most {giftCap} pieces a week.
Exchange: {perExchange} for each offer taken, at most {exchangeCap} exchanges a week.
Help with builds and work: {perHelp} for each help, at most {helpCap} helps a week.
A member gets whole points only, so all the members' Fame together may be a little lower than the guild's.
Donations are the gold and resources given to the Hall's buildings.
“This week” starts on Monday at midnight. “All time” counts from {since}.
members.howWar: Guild war league: Fame for the guild's place in the week's league, shared equally by everyone who fought in its matches.
members.earlier: Earlier donations, from before the game recorded who gave them: {amounts}.

texts.title: Heroes of the week
texts.lead: Every Monday at midnight the System honours the guild's best members of the previous week.
texts.none: Nobody in the guild earned an honour in the previous week.
texts.reward: For each honour you get {timePoints} and a card pack, and a badge shines by your name for the whole week.
how: Guild Pillar: the most Fame brought to the guild, counted as in the members' ranking.
Slayer: the most damage dealt to the Guild Beast and the Guild Expedition's guardians.
Benefactor: the most pieces given to other members in Guild Requests.
Only those in the guild on Monday count. In a tie, the one who has been in the guild longer wins.
For each honour you get {timePoints} and a card pack. The badge by your name shows on the members' list and on your character card until Sunday.

texts.title: Lands under the banner
texts.lead: Each week every land belongs to the guild that spent the most exploration minutes there. On Monday at midnight the winner raises its banner there.
texts.tieWin: Tied with [{tag}]: in a tie the older guild wins, and that is yours
texts.alone: You lead: no other guild has been here yet
texts.tieLose: Tied with [{tag}]: in a tie the older guild wins, so you need one more minute
texts.empty: No guild has explored yet this week. Every minute of your guild brings a banner closer.
texts.noBanners: This week your guild has no banner in any land.
texts.chip: Banner of the guild {name} [{tag}] until Sunday
texts.ownBanner: Your guild's banner: +{bonus}% gold and materials from creatures in this land until Sunday.
texts.otherBanner: The banner of the guild {name} [{tag}] stands here until Sunday.
texts.report: Your guild's banner in this land: +{bonus}% gold and materials from creatures.
how: Every exploration minute counts for the land of the exploration once the member claims the report. On a party trip each member counts their own minutes.
On Monday at midnight the land goes to the guild with the most minutes. In a tie the older guild wins, and where nobody explored there is no banner.
The banner stands for the whole week, and every player sees the guild's tag on the land's card.
For each land the guild gets {fame} of Fame, and its members share it by their minutes in that land.
Members of the guild with the banner get +{bonus}% gold and materials from creatures in that land. From class level 250 the bonus counts from the halved rewards.
texts.howFame: Lands under the banner: {landFame} for each land where the guild raises its banner, in the week it stands.
texts.howMembers: Lands under the banner: {landFame} for a land with the banner, split by the members' minutes in that land.

texts.title: Guild Stall
texts.lead: Every point of Fame you bring the guild gives you one Guild Mark. Spend the Marks here on what you need.
texts.growing: Marks come at once, with every point of Fame.

pack.name: Card pack
pack.description: Three System Deck cards, as at Szczęsny's. Open it in the Games Parlour, on the Cards tab.

ward-scroll.name: Ward Scroll
ward-scroll.description: Guards an item against breaking when you upgrade it on the Anvil from +7.

item.name: An item of your class
item.description: For the equipment slot you choose, at your level, of a rarity as from a champion's chest.

title.name: Title “{title}”
title.description: The title shows in your profile and in the Ranking. Put it on in Achievements, on the Character tab.

frame.name: Banner Frame
frame.description: A portrait frame with the guild banner. Put it on in the System Shop, on the Frames tab.

texts.limitReached: This week's limit is reached. More on Monday.
texts.slotTitle: An item for the slot you choose
texts.slotLead: Choose an equipment slot. You get an item of your class at your level, of a rarity as from a champion's chest.

bought.pack: The card pack waits in the Games Parlour, on the Cards tab.
bought.ward-scroll: You have one more Ward Scroll. Use it on the Anvil.
bought.title: The title “{title}” is yours. Put it on in Achievements, on the Character tab.
bought.frame: The Banner Frame is yours. Put it on in the System Shop, on the Frames tab.

texts.outside: The Guild Stall is for guild members only. Your Marks stay with you and wait until you join a guild.
how: Every point of Fame you bring the guild gives you one Guild Mark at once. Fame counts as in the members' ranking.
Your Marks stay with you after you leave the guild, but the Stall is for members only.
The week's limits renew on Monday at midnight. The title and the frame are bought once.
The item is of your class, at your level and of a rarity as from a champion's chest. It goes into your bag, so it needs room there.

errors.unknown_good: There is no such item for sale.
errors.limit: This week's limit for it is reached. You can buy the next one on Monday.
errors.too_few_marks: You have too few Guild Marks: {marks} of {price}.
errors.bag_full: Your bag is full. Make room in it for the item.
errors.no_guild: The Guild Stall is for guild members only.

ranks.rule: Ranks: R4 the leader, R3 deputies, R2 members, R1 novices. A character new to the guild is a novice for its first {days} days: from the Guild Chest it takes only the items left for it. The leader and the deputies can promote it sooner.
ranks.notNovice: This character is a member already.
